Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the Q3 2024. With me on the call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Taylor Voss, Chief Financial Officer; Morgan Lee, Chief Technology Officer; and Casey Quinn, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud had an exceptional Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

One of our standout achievements was the explosive growth in AI and machine learning workloads on our platform. AI/ML has evolved from an emerging area to our biggest driver of compute revenue, now making up about 28% of our total revenue run-rate, compared to 12% a year ago. Let me share the key metrics and our positioning.

In Q3, AI/ML workloads—including training, fine-tuning, inference, and multimodal apps—surged 162% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter, outpacing our overall infrastructure growth of 42% YoY. We delivered over 1.2 million GPU hours daily, a threefold jump from last year, with 92% peak utilization—our best ever. Training grew 140% YoY but now is 38% of AI/ML compute, down from 55%, while inference exploded 195% YoY to 52%, showing the move to production genAI. The rest, 10%, comes from RAG and agentic workflows.

Our RPO for AI/ML reached $4.2 billion, up 210% YoY, with 65% converting in 12 months, highlighting customer stickiness—like FinTech leader PayNova scaling to petabyte levels. Among top 500 enterprises, 78% run production AI/ML, up 45 points from 2022, with AI customer ARR up 320% to $2.8 million. Our AI Accelerate program for startups saw 250% sign-up growth, 40% paid conversion in 90 days, and 62% of new logos citing AI/ML, versus 22% last year.

Top 10 AI customers, in autonomous driving and drug discovery like Waymo or Recursion analogs, drove 35% of Q3 AI revenue with 5-petabyte storage and 500,000+ H100 GPU hours yearly commitments. Trends include genAI inference demand—our token throughput up 240% YoY to 50 trillion quarterly—multimodal growth at 300% QoQ, and open-source dominance at 68% with PyTorch, Hugging Face, Llama 3.

Supply-wise, NVIDIA Blackwell access helps post-H100 shortages, plus edge AI up 110% YoY. Our NexAI platform, a managed ML service with 25% lower TCO via auto-scaling Spot Instances, launched NexAI Ultra with 16,000 H100s/B200s for 4x FLOPS and 35% faster training; Inference Optimizer for 60% less latency/50% costs on Mistral 7B; and Federated Learning for HIPAA/GDPR. This lifts AI NRR to 148%.

Regionally, US at 52%, EMEA 28% up 135% with sovereign AI in Frankfurt/Paris at 95% utilization, APAC 18% exploding 285% via India/Japan, LatAm up 180%. We're ahead of AWS/Azure with multi-model support, 20% cheaper GPUs, $2.5B FY24 capex ($1.2B AI infra) to 50,000 GPUs. Partners: NVIDIA Co-Sell, Arm Neoverse, Hugging Face.

FY25 guide: 110-130% growth, inference to 65%, with renewable PUE 1.15 mitigating risks. This redefines our economics.

Now I'll turn the call over to Taylor Voss to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Voss:
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in Q3. Revenue grew by 28% year-over-year to $27.5 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 32.5%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 28%.

Today, I'd like to unpack our Cloud Services gross margin, which expanded 310 basis points YoY to 32.4%. This is revenue minus costs like data centers, depreciation, power, bandwidth—divided by revenue. It matches top peers like AWS at 33%, Azure 31%, thanks to hyperscale and AI demand.

First, scale: 42 regions, 12 million servers, 86% utilization up from 81%, via AetherPredict AI forecasting. Each 5pp utilization adds 100-150bps; Q3 added 180bps. Expect 88-90% by year-end.

Second, mix: IaaS down to 38% mix (low-20s margins), PaaS like NexAI up 65% to 24% (45%+ margins), SaaS/K8s/serverless 38% (40%+). GenAI drove 15% growth, inference 75% YoY.

Third, efficiencies: NexaraCore ARM chips at 55% capacity, 25% better perf/watt, cutting energy 8%; AetherOS optimizations up density 18%; bandwidth renegos down 10%. Offset 14% energy rise.

Regionally: NA 52% rev at 35.2%; EMEA 22% at 30.1%; APAC 18% at 28.5%; LatAm 26%. Headwinds: 3% ASP erosion, $18B AI capex (90bps hit), countered by Spot at 15% compute (60% discount).

Outlook: 200bps to 34-35% FY25 with AI 25% mix, 90% util, NexaraCore 3.0, 60% renewables. $150B RPO up 42%, 70% high-margin.

Now, I'll hand it over to Morgan Lee for a technical update.

Morgan Lee:
Thank you, Taylor. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new NexAI platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

Turning to our network performance and reliability metrics, these form the foundation of our hyperscale infrastructure. In cloud, where AI H100 clusters or SAP HANA need sub-ms precision, they drive retention and ARPU. Our $2.8B backbone investment shines through.

Global SLA: 99.999% (five nines, <5.26 min/year downtime), 100% compliance, up 10bps YoY via AI failover. Beats AWS 99.99%, Azure. Latency: global 42ms avg (15% QoQ/28% YoY better), intra-region <8ms, jitter <1ms 99th, loss 0.0003%. Throughput: 12.5Gbps avg ApexDirect, 100Gbps bursts, 450Tbps backbone, 1.2ZB Q3 transfer up 42% YoY.

Reliability: MTTR 4.2 min P1 (from 7.1), via GenAI anomaly detection preempting 78%; MTBF 2M hours routers; DDoS absorbed 15Tbps peak. Network Health Score up 22%.

Initiatives: 1,200 edge POPs (300 new), 35% last-mile cut for 5G MEC; SDN/NFV with SONiC zero-touch, 40% orch latency down; C+L optics on APEX-1 subsea 3x capacity low-power.

Regions: NA 52% rev, 99.9999% six nines, 6ms; EMEA 28% 38ms; APAC 15% 52ms improving; LATAM 99.99%. UltraReliable tier 25% premium, 18% rev growth driver.

Future: $750M FY25 for terabit Ethernet/AI maintenance, 99.9999% SLA, <30ms latency for 30% workload growth.

I'll now pass it to Casey Quinn for a product roadmap update.

Casey Quinn:
Thank you, Morgan. This quarter, we launched NexAI Ultra, a game-changing solution for enterprise AI workloads. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

As part of our roadmap, energy efficiency and sustainability are core to our product innovations, supporting revenue growth to $27.5 billion while targeting the $1.2T sustainable cloud TAM by 2030. Investors love our ESG leadership in data centers using 2-3% global power.

Metrics: Fleet PUE 1.12 (from 1.18, below 1.5 benchmark), 22% less energy/1k hours, $187M power savings (8% OpEx); 68% renewables (from 52%), 78% 24/7 carbon-free NA/EU.

Roadmap: Liquid cooling in 12 sites, 40% less cooling, WUE 0.15 in VA/OR; Nexara Graviton4 ARM 40% workloads, 25% perf/watt, 18% idle cut; Broadcom TPUs 50% less for LLM training; Blackwell liquid racks 2.5x density 15% less power.

Regions: EU Nordics PUE 1.08 100% hydro/wind PPAs Vattenfall, $2.4B ARR SAP/Siemens; APAC 55% solar Rajasthan Adani, Singapore ocean-cooled WUE~0; US IRA $450M credits, Texas wind/nuclear NuScale, Ohio 85% carbon-free 120gCO2e/kWh.

Moat: 35% Q3 bookings ESG-cited, Unilever/Pfizer wins; 2.2pts margin expansion, +150bps FY25. $5.2B CapEx 18% green, Carbon Intelligence ML shifts loads; targets PUE<1.10 '26, 100% RE '30, net-zero '28. Partners Ørsted, Cloud Carbon Coalition.

Efficiency is profitability—de-risks power prices up 12%, appeals 62% enterprises.

Now, back to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Casey. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

Strategically, our pricing strategies and discounting have been pivotal. In this competitive space—AWS 31%, Azure 25%, GCP 11%—pricing drives acquisition/retention while guarding 28% op margin.

Effective pricing $0.047/core-hour, down 4.2% YoY, but consumption rev up 32% to 68% mix, NRR 128%, top 1k ARPU +15%. RIs/Savings Plans 62% compute (72% off), +$1.2B ARR; Spot 18% usage sub-$0.01, 72% margins.

Enterprise EAs: 18-22% rebates for >10k vCPU AI, AI rev $2.4B +78% 22% total; GPU $3.85/hr vs AWS $4.10, 14% share. NA 52% rev 3.1% compression ARPU $4.2M +12%; APAC 28% rev 41% growth 7.5% deeper discounts, $500k credits +60% logos; EMEA sovereign 15% off €300M telco.

New Nexara FlexiCommit 55-65% discounts ML-flexible, 20% adoption lift. FY25 compression 2-3% with AI +15%, Green Reservations 5% off. Grow 25-30% rev, margins >27%.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Jordan, the AI/ML numbers sound impressive—can you give more color on customer adoption trends and how that impacts FY25 guidance?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, adoption is accelerating across enterprises and startups, with 78% of top customers in production and new logos prioritizing AI. This visibility from $4.2B RPO gives us confidence in 110-130% growth next year, focusing on inference scaling. We're positioned well with NexAI differentiators.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
Thanks. Taylor, on gross margins, with AI capex ramping, how are you balancing investments with the 200bps expansion outlook? Any more on pricing pressures?

Taylor Voss:
Great question, Sarah. Our utilization push to 90% and high-margin AI/PaaS shift more than offset capex, with efficiencies like ARM chips helping. Pricing held resilient, modest 3% erosion countered by premium tiers—expect steady expansion as scale kicks in.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with RBC Capital. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Thanks, team. Morgan, with AI workloads exploding, how is network reliability holding up, and any updates on edge expansions?

Morgan Lee:
Hi Mike. Our 99.999% SLA and 42ms latency improvements handle the surge seamlessly, with GenAI prediction preempting issues. Edge POPs at 1,200 now cut latency 35% for MEC/AI, supporting 30% growth ahead.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in Nexara Cloud. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
